packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

PACKET-04 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (isolated first reader)

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this item. This is a blind reading. I have not tried to identify work or author.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON QUALITY: this is a very rapid, heavily abbreviated cursive in grey ink on stained paper, and on face 1 most of the upper half has pen lines drawn along or through the writing. I read every tile slowly. What follows is a partial reading: secure words and phrases are given plainly, doubtful ones carry "?", and much is [illegible]. I estimate that I read securely well under half of the words on face 1 and roughly half on face 2. The gaps on the upper half of face 1 are partly a property of the leaf (overdrawn lines, stains) and partly a limit of my reading of this hand; a second reader should not treat my [illegible] there as proof that the text is lost.

Conventions: (..) = my expansion; ? after a word = uncertain; [illegible] = not read; [..] = lost or not read part of a word. Abbreviations of the hand that I resolved consistently once recognised: a 9-shaped sign + "riis/ria" = c(ontr)ariis / c(ontr)aria; "sbto" with stroke = sub(iec)to; "ho" with stroke = h(om)o; single stroke = e(st); "n" with stroke = n(on). Line numbers are counted from the top of each named tile and are approximate, because the lines slope and tiles begin mid-line.

=====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
=====================================================================
Two overviews, each one face of a single upright leaf about 11 x 17.5 cm by the ruler:
- image-001 = face 1 (tiles image-002 to image-011, in pairs left/right, top to bottom).
- image-012 = face 2 (tiles image-013 to image-022, in pairs left/right, top to bottom).
Observed: single column, long lines, no ruling visible, about 45-50 lines per face, lines sloping and crowded; text runs to the very top edge on both faces, so the leaf may be trimmed or the text begins mid-entry. Small holes along both vertical edges and scattered through the leaf; corners clipped; brown stains throughout. No running titles, no rubrics, no coloured or enlarged initials, no marginal glosses seen. Text is in paragraphs separated by blank space: face 1 has a large upper block and, after a clear gap, a lower block of about 14 lines; face 2 has a short block of about 5 lines at the top, a long middle block, and after a gap a last block of about 11 lines. Several lines begin with an indent or leave a blank space inside the line (apparently new sentences/sections started mid-line). 
Face 1, upper block: many long horizontal pen strokes run along the lines, in places clearly through the letters and in places beneath them. I cannot tell from the images whether this is cancellation of whole passages or heavy underlining; I think cancellation is more likely for at least some groups of lines (tentative).
A few words are cancelled individually (noted below).
Tentative interpretation (not observation): continuous school notes in prose, proceeding by short sections each on a "locus a ..." with a definition, an example argument and a stated "maxima"; no separate lemma/commentary structure seen.

Areas selected: face 1 lower block (best preserved, read almost line by line); face 2 top block, parts of the middle block, and the last block. Face 1 upper block is given only as isolated phrases.
